kurz: In alkaline conditions the [[maillard-reaktion|Maillard reaction]] runs much faster. That is why pretzels turn deep brown and onions with a pinch of baking soda darken faster.
bild_im_kopf: Like a tailwind on a bike: the route is the same, but you get there much faster.
was_passiert: The browning reaction depends on the [[ph-wert|pH]]. Acid slows it down; alkalis such as baking soda or lye speed it up a lot. Pretzels are dipped briefly in a lye bath before baking: the surface then browns deeply, shines and gets its typical taste. A pinch of baking soda makes onions brown and soften faster; too much tastes soapy.
warum_wichtig: Explains the colour of pretzels and lye rolls, and why a hint of baking soda saves time when frying.
faustregeln: For onions, a pinch of baking soda on the tip of a knife, no more.
Acid such as lemon or wine slows browning, so add it later.
Real food-grade lye is caustic: gloves, goggles, nothing made of aluminium.

praxis.text: Pretzel: dipped briefly in lye, then baked. At home, baked baking soda gives a milder version.
Onions with baking soda turn golden brown in half the time.
